question: After a final MCAD finding that a licensee violated Chapter 151B, the Board must suspend the license for:
optionB: 60 days
explanation: Under M.G.L. c. 112, section 87AAA, a final MCAD finding of a Chapter 151B violation requires the Board to suspend the license for 60 days. The 90-day suspension applies only to a second violation within two years of a prior one.

question: Before suspending or revoking a license, the Board must give the licensee written notice of a hearing at least:
optionB: 7 days before
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87BBB requires a hearing with at least ten days' written notice, including the grounds, before a license is suspended or revoked. Twenty days is the time an aggrieved licensee has to appeal the decision to the superior court.

question: How many classroom hours of approved real estate courses must a Massachusetts salesperson applicant complete before the exam?
optionB: 40 hours
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87SS requires approved courses totaling 40 classroom hours before a salesperson applicant may take the exam. Brokers need another 40 hours plus three years as an active salesperson.

question: An original Massachusetts salesperson license issued to an individual remains valid until:
optionA: Second anniversary of the license issue date
optionB: December 31 of the second year after issue
optionC: Licensee's birthday falling more than 12 months after issue
optionD: Licensee's birthday falling more than 24 months after issue
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87XX makes an original individual license valid until the anniversary of the licensee's date of birth next occurring more than 24 months after issue. Renewals then run two years at a time, so the license always expires on the birthday.

question: A Massachusetts licensee on inactive status may still:
optionA: Receive referral fees for procuring prospects
optionB: Negotiate leases for an affiliated broker
optionC: Host open houses for the former brokerage
optionD: Present offers to clients already under contract
explanation: Under M.G.L. c. 112, section 87XX 1/2, an inactive licensee is treated as unlicensed but may assist in procuring prospects and receive referral fees. Negotiating, hosting showings or presenting offers is acting as a broker or salesperson and can lead to revocation.

question: The education certificate a Massachusetts salesperson candidate uses to qualify for the exam is valid for:
optionB: 18 months
explanation: 254 CMR 2.00(3) limits the education certification to 24 months after the education was completed, and the PSI bulletin says the exam must be passed within that two-year period. A partial pass expires with the certificate.

question: Under Board rules, every advertisement a licensee places to sell or rent a home must include:
optionB: Commission rate charged to the seller
optionD: Name of the real estate broker
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(9)(a) requires every advertisement to include the name of the real estate broker and to disclose that the advertiser is a broker. The rule also bars ads that show only a post office box, phone number or street address.

question: A Massachusetts salesperson may lawfully accept a commission for a sale from:
optionA: Only the broker the salesperson is affiliated with
optionB: Seller directly, if the listing agreement allows it
optionC: Buyer directly, if the buyer agrees to it in writing
optionD: Any broker who cooperated on the sale
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, sections 87RR and 87VV bar a salesperson from accepting any fee or commission from anyone except the licensed broker with whom the salesperson is affiliated. A salesperson also may not be affiliated with more than one broker at a time.

question: A seller wants $400,000 and lets the broker keep anything above it. In Massachusetts this arrangement is:
optionA: Allowed with the seller's written consent
optionB: Allowed if the price is disclosed to buyers
optionC: Allowed only for vacant land sales
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87AAA(l) and 254 CMR 3.00(11)(c) prohibit accepting a net listing, in which the broker keeps any amount over a stated price. Written consent does not cure it, because the commission is left unspecified.

question: An unlicensed person finds a buyer for a Massachusetts home after the owner promised a fee. In court, that person:
optionA: Cannot recover the fee without a broker's license
optionB: Can recover the fee if the owner's promise was in writing
optionC: Can recover the fee if the sale closed
optionD: Can recover the fee after licensing later
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87RR bars any suit in Massachusetts courts for broker compensation unless the person was a licensed broker when the services were performed. A written promise or a later license does not change that.

question: Massachusetts rules require the Board's agency disclosure notice to be given to a prospective buyer or seller at the:
optionA: Signing of the purchase and sale agreement for the home
optionB: Submission of the buyer's first written offer
optionC: First telephone call with the consumer
optionD: First personal meeting to discuss a specific property
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(13)(a) requires the notice at the first personal meeting between the licensee and the prospective buyer or seller to discuss a specific property. The licensee asks for a signature and keeps a copy for three years, or notes that the consumer declined to sign.

question: A salesperson is listing a house owned by her brother. Under Board rules she must:
optionA: Disclose it in writing and get written acknowledgment
optionB: Disclose it orally to every party before any offer
optionC: Get written approval from her broker and the Board
optionD: Refer the listing to a broker at another firm
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(11)(a) bars a licensee from representing a client in a sale in which the licensee or kin has a personal financial interest unless the interest is fully disclosed in writing to all parties and they acknowledge it in writing. Oral disclosure to one party is not enough.

question: Under the Massachusetts rental law effective August 1, 2025, a broker's fee for finding an apartment is paid by:
optionA: Incoming tenant in every rental transaction
optionB: Landlord and tenant in equal shares
optionD: Only the party who engaged the broker
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87DDD 1/2, as amended effective August 1, 2025, lets a broker contract solely with a tenant or solely with a landlord, and any fee is paid only by the party who originally engaged the broker. A landlord's broker can no longer pass the fee to the tenant.

question: Under the Massachusetts dual agency consent form, a dual agent still owes both clients the duties of:
optionB: Undivided loyalty and full disclosure of information
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(13)(b) says a dual agent cannot fully satisfy loyalty, full disclosure, reasonable care and obedience, but still owes confidentiality of material information and the duty to account for funds. Undivided loyalty to both sides is impossible when their interests conflict.

question: When a broker appoints designated agents for both the buyer and the seller, Massachusetts presumes the appointing broker is a:
optionB: Subagent
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87AAA 3/4(c) and 254 CMR 3.00(13)(c) presume the appointing broker to be a dual agent when designated agents represent both sides. The designated agents themselves each represent only their own client.

question: Under Massachusetts rules, a non-agent facilitator does NOT owe the buyer or seller:
optionB: Disclosure of known material defects in the property
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(13)(e) gives a facilitator the duties to present property honestly, disclose known material defects and account for funds, but no duty of confidentiality. The facilitator must give written notice that no agency relationship exists at the first personal meeting.

question: Under Board rules, a written offer on a property a licensee has the right to sell must reach the owner:
optionB: Forthwith
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(11)(d) requires all offers to be conveyed forthwith to the owner. A set grace period such as 48 hours or three business days is not in the rule.

question: Unless the parties agree otherwise in writing, a Massachusetts broker holding a buyer's deposit must:
optionA: Deposit it in the brokerage operating account
optionB: Hold it in the office safe until closing
optionC: Deposit it immediately in a bank escrow account
optionD: Deposit it within ten days in any bank account it chooses
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(10)(a) requires money held during a transaction to be deposited immediately in a bank escrow account, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing. Putting it in the operating account would be commingling.

question: A buyer with no buyer's agency agreement asks the listing agent to name a home inspector. The agent may:
optionA: Recommend the one inspector the agent personally trusts most
optionB: Refer the buyer to the agent's relative
optionC: Choose and book the inspection for the buyer
optionD: Provide the Board's complete list of licensed inspectors
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87YY 1/2 bars brokers and salespersons from directly recommending a specific home inspector, but they may provide the Board's complete list on request. The ban does not apply to a broker acting exclusively for the buyer under a written agreement or disclosure.

question: Under Massachusetts license law, a licensee must give a copy of the purchase and sale agreement to:
optionA: Both the buyer and the seller
optionB: Only the seller who signed it
explanation: M.G.L. c. 112, section 87AAA(i) makes failing to give both the buyer and the seller a copy of the purchase and sale agreement a ground for discipline. Giving it to one party or to the lender alone does not satisfy the law.

question: After a tenant signs a lease the landlord agreed to execute, Massachusetts requires a fully signed copy within:
optionB: 14 days
explanation: M.G.L. c. 186, section 15D requires a lessor who obtains the tenant's signature to deliver a copy signed by the lessor within thirty days. A lease clause waiving this requirement is void.

question: Massachusetts Board rules state that a broker or salesperson may never:
optionA: Explain how a mortgage contingency works
optionB: Advise against the use of an attorney
optionC: Share recent comparable sales with a seller
optionD: Suggest the buyer get a loan preapproval
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(12) bars any broker or salesperson from advising against the use of an attorney in any real property transaction. Explaining contract terms or sharing market data is ordinary brokerage work.

question: Before suing a business under Chapter 93A, a consumer generally must send a written demand for relief at least:
optionB: 30 days before filing
explanation: M.G.L. c. 93A, section 9(3) requires a written demand for relief at least thirty days before filing. A business that makes a reasonable written settlement offer within that time can limit its recovery to the offer.

question: If a court finds a willful or knowing Chapter 93A violation, the consumer's actual damages are multiplied by:
optionA: Exactly one and a half times
optionB: Up to five but not less than four times
optionC: Up to three but not less than two times
explanation: M.G.L. c. 93A, section 9(3) allows up to three but not less than two times actual damages for a willful or knowing violation, or a bad-faith refusal to grant relief. Without willfulness, recovery is actual damages or $25, whichever is greater.

question: A brokerage that owns client data learns of a breach. Besides affected residents, Massachusetts law requires notice to:
optionA: Board of Registration and the local multiple listing service
optionB: Federal Trade Commission and local police
optionC: Secretary of the Commonwealth and the bank
optionD: Attorney General and the director of consumer affairs
explanation: M.G.L. c. 93H, section 3(b) requires a person that owns or licenses the data to notify the Attorney General, the director of consumer affairs and business regulation, and the affected residents. The real estate board is not a named recipient.

question: A designated seller's agent may not share information that would harm the seller's interest, except:
optionA: Known material defects in the property
optionB: Lowest price the seller will accept
optionD: Offers the seller has already rejected
explanation: 254 CMR 3.00(13)(c)1 bars a designated agent from sharing information that would harm the client, except known material defects, which the agent has an affirmative obligation to disclose. The seller's lowest price stays confidential.

question: Massachusetts requires a seller to give a buyer the property transfer lead paint notification:
optionA: At the closing table with the deed
optionB: Before the purchase and sale agreement is signed
optionC: Within ten days after the offer
optionD: Only if a child under six will live in the home
explanation: M.G.L. c. 111, section 197A requires sellers to give prospective purchasers the state lead notification form before the purchase and sale agreement is signed, and any agent must get the buyer's signed certification. Massachusetts lead abatement duties turn on children under six, but the notice goes to every buyer.

question: Under Title 5, a septic system serving a home being sold must generally be inspected at or within:
optionB: 2 years before the transfer
explanation: 310 CMR 15.301(1) requires inspection at or within two years before transfer of title, or up to three years with records of annual pumping. If weather prevents it, the inspection may be done up to six months after transfer with written notice to the buyer.

question: When a Massachusetts home is sold, which party must equip it with approved smoke detectors?
optionB: Listing broker
explanation: M.G.L. c. 148, section 26F requires the seller to equip a residential building with approved smoke detectors upon sale or transfer. The head of the local fire department enforces the requirement.

question: In most Massachusetts towns, the riverfront area extends from a river's mean annual high-water line:
optionB: 100 feet
explanation: 310 CMR 10.58(2) sets the riverfront area at 200 feet from the mean annual high-water line, but only 25 feet in listed cities such as Boston and in designated densely developed areas. The 100-foot figure is the buffer zone around other wetland resource areas.

question: A Massachusetts landlord refuses an applicant because she would pay with a Section 8 voucher. This is:
optionA: Lawful if the policy is applied to every applicant
optionB: Lawful in owner-occupied buildings
explanation: M.G.L. c. 151B, section 4(10) makes it unlawful to discriminate against a tenant who receives federal, state or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance, because of that subsidy. The federal Fair Housing Act does not list source of income.

question: The Massachusetts ban on refusing to rent to families with children does NOT apply to leasing:
optionA: One unit of an owner-occupied two-family house
optionB: Any unit in a nonowner-occupied three-family building
optionC: Any unit in a building built before 1978
optionD: Furnished units in a large complex
explanation: M.G.L. c. 151B, section 4(11) exempts leasing a unit in a two-family dwelling whose other unit the owner occupies. A pre-1978 building is not exempt; refusing families because of lead paint is itself unlawful.

question: Which class is protected under Massachusetts housing law but not listed in the federal Fair Housing Act?
optionB: Genetic information
explanation: M.G.L. c. 151B, section 4(6) adds classes such as genetic information, ancestry, marital status, age and veteran status. National origin, disability and sex are protected under both laws.

question: An owner rents out her own condo for ten months while abroad. Under the Massachusetts children rule, this rental is:
optionB: Exempt only with MCAD approval
explanation: M.G.L. c. 151B, section 4(11) exempts the temporary leasing of a single dwelling, apartment or condominium unit the owner ordinarily occupies, during an absence of not more than one year.

question: At the start of a Massachusetts residential tenancy, a security deposit may not exceed:
optionB: One and a half months' rent
explanation: M.G.L. c. 186, section 15B(1)(b) limits upfront charges to first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent and the cost of a new lock and key. The deposit must go in a separate, interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account.

question: A landlord who accepts a security deposit must give the tenant a written statement of condition within:
optionB: 10 days
explanation: M.G.L. c. 186, section 15B(2)(c) requires the statement on receipt of the deposit or within ten days after the tenancy starts, whichever is later. Fifteen days is the time the tenant has to return it with any added damage.

question: After a Massachusetts tenancy ends, the landlord must return the security deposit, less lawful deductions, within:
optionB: 21 days
explanation: M.G.L. c. 186, section 15B(4) requires the deposit, with interest and less lawful deductions, to be returned within thirty days after the tenancy ends. Failing to return it can cost the landlord three times the amount owed.

question: Under the State Sanitary Code, daytime heat in a habitable room during the heating season must be at least:
optionB: 65 degrees F
explanation: 105 CMR 410.180 requires at least 68 degrees F from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. and 64 degrees F overnight, from September 15 through May 31. The 64-degree figure is the nighttime minimum.

question: Title to registered land in Massachusetts can NOT be acquired against the registered owner by:
optionB: Devise in the owner's will
explanation: M.G.L. c. 185, section 53 provides that no title, easement or other right in registered land can be acquired by prescription or adverse possession. Deeds and wills still transfer registered land through the Land Court system.

question: A Massachusetts condo owner pays the fee and requests a 6(d) statement in writing. When is it due?
optionB: 10 business days
explanation: Under Massachusetts General Laws, chapter 183A, section 6(d), the association has ten business days after receiving the written request. The usual fee is waived for a mortgagee that has notified the association of its intent to foreclose.
